title: Needless Independent Persistence for Owner-Local Values
pattern: Small, owner-local value objects or primitive collections are modeled as independently identified tables/entities despite being read and changed with their owner.
why_bad: Artificial entity identities and joins add storage, retrieval, and mapping work without serving the domain model: every load of the owner pays for extra joins or ORM round-trips to reassemble a few attributes that are always read and modified together.
detection: An ORM mapping or schema adds child/join tables or surrogate identities for values with no independent identity or lifecycle, and the resulting joins provide no required query, constraint, sharing, or update benefit. Two subcases: (a) a scalar value object with a few cohesive attributes (e.g., address, coordinates, a benefit/cost rating) declared as its own relation with an auto-incremented surrogate key; (b) a simple multi-valued collection (e.g., strings or integers such as phone numbers or skill names) declared as a one-to-many join table with per-row primary keys.
counterexample: Rich, independently mutable entities with their own identity and lifecycle; globally shared reference data (e.g., a standard postal-code list); values that are very large or shared across millions of owners (e.g., product images); elements that must be separately indexed, constrained, or queried on their own. Identity-free values alone do not make a child table wrong when query or constraint requirements justify it. `Contextual`.
fix: Embed scalar value-object attributes as typed owner columns using the ORM's value/embedded mapping. For genuinely owner-local collections, use a database-native array or structured JSON column that preserves element boundaries (not a comma-separated string) if it preserves the required semantics. Keep separate relations when independent querying, integrity constraints, cardinality, or lifecycle requires them.
source: *Domain-Driven Design*, Chapter 5, Value Objects (p. 348) and *Implementing Domain-Driven Design*, Chapter 7 (p. 500); *Implementing Domain-Driven Design (Vernon), p. 471 [242, 528]*; *Implementing Domain-Driven Design (Vernon), Chapter 6, p. 225-227, 249 [225-227, 673]*; *Implementing Domain-Driven Design (Vernon), Chapter 6, p. 227 [227, 1058]*
